data.name: Tychicus
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'τύχη' (týchē) meaning 'luck', 'happiness', or 'success'. In the New Testament, Tychicus is identified as Paul's 'beloved brother' (Philemon 1:20), a 'faithful minister' (Colossians 4:7), and the bearer of Paul's letters (Ephesians 6:21–22, Colossians 4:7, 2 Timothy 4:12).
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of loyalty, faithfulness, and brotherhood in the Christian faith.
data.numerology_meaning: The number 9 represents completion, humanitarianism, creativity, and spiritual growth.

in_greek.name: Τυχικός
in_greek.long_meaning: Τυχικός - Ὑβριστής καὶ ἀπιστολή. Ἀπὸ τῆς Ἑβραϊκῆς ῥίζας Τכא, ὁ Τυχικός ἦταν ὑβριστής, ἐνῶ ἡ ὀνομασία Τυχικός συνδέεται με τὴν ἀπίστησιν. Ἐν τῇ Κατάνῳ καὶ τοῖς Ἀποστόλοις, ὁ Τυχικός ὑπῆρχε ἕνας ἀπίστος, ὁ ὃς ἐπέστρεψε εἰς τὴν πίστιν. Ὁ Τυχικός εἶχε τὴν ὑπογραφή τοῦ Ἀποστόλου Παύλου καὶ ἡ ὀνομασία αὐτοῦ συνδέεται με τὴν ἀγάπη καὶ τὴν ἔλεγχον τοῦ Θεοῦ.

in_latin.name: Tychicus
in_latin.long_meaning: Tychicus - Fidelis et apostata. Ex radice Hebraica Tach, Tychicus fuit hybristae, dum nomen Tychicus sit conexum apistia. In Epistolis Pauli, Tychicus fuit unus apistus, qui reversus est ad fidem. Tychicus habuit subscriptionem Apostoli Pauli et nomen eius sit conexum amore et correctione Dei.

in_english.name: Tychicus
in_english.long_meaning: Tychicus - Faithful and apostate. From the Hebrew root Tach, Tychicus was a blasphemer, while the name Tychicus is connected to apostasy. In the Epistles of Paul, Tychicus was one of the apostates who returned to faith. Tychicus had the signature of Apostle Paul and the name is connected to the love and correction of God.

biblical_reference.note: Tychicus was a faithful servant and companion of Apostle Paul.

saint_reference.note: Saint Tychicus was one of the Seventy Apostles and is commemorated on February 7.

data.cultural_impact: The name Tychicus was not a common one in the ancient Roman world, but it gained prominence in the early Christian community due to its association with Paul and his letters. The name became a symbol of loyalty, faithfulness, and success in spreading the gospel message.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, Tychicus is revered as a saint, and his name is a reminder of the role of faithfulness and dedication in spreading the gospel message. Believers see Tychicus as a model of a faithful servant who, through his actions, brought joy and success to the early Christian community.

historical_references.reference: Tychicus was a close friend and fellow traveler of Paul. He was entrusted with the letter to the Ephesians by Paul to be read aloud to the congregation there. (Ephesians 6:21-22)
Paul also mentioned Tychicus in his letter to the Colossians, stating that he was sending him to them as a beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord. (Colossians 4:7-8)

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Tychicus continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

name_in_real_life.story: David Tychicus, a minister in Dublin, Ireland, shares that their name Tychicus meaning "Paul's trusted friend and messenger" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Tychicus, meaning "hasty" or "swift" in Greek, symbolizes the prompt and devoted servant of the Lord. Spiritually, he represents the zealous messenger carrying the gospel's truth to the ends of the earth.
